# Code of conduct

Mongla is built in the open so that people can learn from it, argue with it and improve it.
That works only if everyone can take part without being made to feel small.

## What we expect

- Argue with the measurement, not the person. "This number does not support that claim" is
  welcome; anything aimed at someone's ability, background or identity is not.
- Assume good faith, and say what you would do instead.
- Credit people's work, including the sources a change drew on.
- Be patient with newcomers. Every one of us once asked what a Kalman filter was.

## What is not acceptable

Harassment, insults, sexualised language or imagery, threats, publishing someone's private
information, and sustained disruption of discussions, issues or pull requests.

## Scope and enforcement

This applies in the repository, its issues, pull requests, discussions and wiki, and wherever
someone represents the project. Report a problem privately: GitHub's **Report content** on
the comment itself, or a private report from this repository's **Security** tab with
"conduct" in the title, which only the maintainer sees. Reports are kept confidential. The maintainer may
remove content, and warn, suspend or ban a participant, in proportion to what happened.

Adapted in spirit from the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/).
